description: The National Fire Department Registry is the U.S. Fire Administration's list of fire departments in the United States, compiled from departments that register themselves. Each entry gives the Fire Department Identifier (FDID), name, headquarters and mailing address, county, department type (career, combination or volunteer), organisation type, number of stations, counts of active career, volunteer and paid-per-call firefighters and of non-firefighting staff, and whether the department is the primary emergency management agency; a station file lists every station address. The producer is the U.S. Fire Administration, part of FEMA. Coverage is national, about 27,000 department rows in the national file read today. Files are CSV, downloadable nationally or by state from the registry web application without registration; no licence is stated, as a federal work. Caveats: registration is voluntary, so some departments are missing or out of date; station addresses are not geocoded; staffing counts are self-reported. Simulation uses: an inventory of fire and rescue capacity for coverage and response-time models, location-allocation of stations, and surge planning when stations sit in hazard zones. Related records: HIFLD Open (data-hifld-open) carries geocoded fire and EMS station layers, and NFIRS (data-usfa-nfirs-public-data-release) uses the same FDID keys.
